disclaimer: Ask Navigator creates a starting workflow, not a validated experimental design. Outputs listed here are planned, not generated. Check instrument support, sample preparation, QC, statistical design, annotation confidence and database coverage before analysis.

stages.title: Starting data
stages.question: What are you starting with?
stages.intro: This first route covers untargeted small-molecule LC-MS data and processed LC-MS abundance tables. Your data stay with you; this planner does not upload or analyze files.

options.label: LC-MS instrument files
options.why: Start with the original files and plan import or conversion.
options.input: Vendor LC-MS files
options.output: Raw files retained for processing and sharing

options.label: LC-MS files already in mzML
options.why: Open-format spectra can enter compatible feature-processing workflows.
options.input: LC-MS mzML files
options.output: mzML retained for processing and sharing

options.label: A processed LC-MS abundance table
options.why: Start downstream when features have already been aligned across samples.
options.input: Feature-by-sample abundances with unique feature and sample identifiers
options.output: Feature table to review; no linked MS/MS is assumed

options.label: GC-MS, imaging, targeted MS or other data
options.why: Find guidance for your data without forcing it into an untargeted LC-MS route.
options.input: An acquisition or analysis type outside this alpha route
options.output: A clarification checklist rather than an incompatible workflow

blocker.title: This data type needs a different route.
blocker.nextAction: Record the analytical platform, acquisition mode, starting files and study question. Use the Guide to choose a specialist route; this alpha currently supports untargeted LC-MS only.

stages.title: Acquisition
stages.question: What fragmentation data were collected?
stages.intro: DDA selects individual precursor ions for fragmentation. DIA fragments wider windows or all ions and needs a different processing route. Check the acquisition method with your operator if unsure.

options.label: High-resolution LC-MS/MS with DDA
options.why: Data-dependent acquisition provides precursor-linked fragments for the curated annotation route.
options.input: Accurate-mass MS1 and DDA MS/MS from small molecules
options.output: Plan to retain precursor and fragment information
options.caution: Confirm acquisition mode and mass accuracy. This route does not cover undeconvoluted DIA spectra.

options.label: MS1 only, or no usable MS/MS
options.why: Feature processing and statistical comparisons remain possible without a fragmentation route.
options.input: LC-MS data without usable precursor-linked fragments
options.output: An abundance-focused plan

options.label: DIA or all-ion fragmentation
options.why: These spectra need appropriate deconvolution and precursor assignment before a feature-linked MS/MS route.
options.input: LC-MS DIA or all-ion data
options.output: A specialist processing review before annotation or networking

blocker.title: DIA needs its own reviewed route.
blocker.nextAction: Confirm the instrument and DIA mode, then review a compatible deconvolution workflow. Do not submit unassigned all-ion spectra to the DDA path. This alpha does not yet plan DIA processing.

options.label: I need to check the acquisition mode
options.why: Confirm the acquisition before choosing a compatible processing and annotation route.
options.input: Acquisition details to confirm with the operator
options.output: Questions to resolve with the instrument operator
options.caution: Confirm LC-MS acquisition details before implementing the plan; revisit this choice once known.

blocker.title: Confirm your acquisition mode first.
blocker.nextAction: Ask the operator: was this LC-MS, was MS/MS collected, was it DDA or DIA/all-ion, and were accurate-mass precursor and fragment spectra acquired? Keep the original files and method. Return here once you know.

stages.title: Import / conversion
stages.question: How will you open your instrument files?
stages.intro: Converting a file changes its representation; it does not detect or align features.

options.label: Convert to mzML with MSConvert
options.why: Prepare an open-format input for the processing choices that follow.
options.input: A supported vendor format
options.output: mzML spectra
options.caution: Some vendor readers need Windows. Confirm reader support and preserve centroiding/filter settings and original files.

options.label: Use a processor's supported direct import
options.why: MZmine and MS-DIAL offer direct readers for supported vendor formats.
options.input: Vendor files supported by the selected processor and operating system
options.output: Files available to the processor
options.caution: Direct import is conditional on vendor, version and operating system. If unsupported, go back and plan conversion to mzML.

stages.title: Feature processing
stages.question: Which processing environment suits you?
stages.intro: Turn signals into a table that can be compared across samples. This is usually called feature detection and alignment. Each option is an alternative, not a ranking.

options.label: MZmine · graphical workflow
options.why: Graphical processing can retain feature-linked MS/MS and export downstream files.
options.input: Supported vendor files or mzML
options.output: Aligned feature table; for the DDA route, separately export matched MGF/MSP spectra
options.caution: Use the dedicated downstream export settings and matching feature identifiers. Verify current access terms and inspect processing parameters.

options.label: MS-DIAL · graphical workflow
options.why: Provides feature processing and spectral export with integrated annotation options.
options.input: Supported vendor files or mzML
options.output: Aligned feature table; for the DDA route, separately export matched MGF/MSP spectra
options.caution: Check export conventions and preserve feature IDs. An integrated library match does not establish a fully resolved structure.

options.label: XCMS · scripted R workflow
options.why: R/Bioconductor supports reproducible feature processing and alignment.
options.input: mzML plus sample metadata
options.output: Aligned feature abundance table
options.caution: This initial route covers table export only. It does not assume an XCMS feature-linked MS/MS export; networking is therefore omitted.

stages.title: Quality-control plan
stages.question: Include a quality-control review before interpretation.
stages.intro: A feature table can contain background, drift and unreliable signals. This is a planning checkpoint, not a claim that your data have passed QC.

options.label: Add QC and sample-metadata review
options.why: Review blanks, pooled QC where available, missingness, alignment and sample labels before comparing groups.
options.input: Feature table, acquisition order, study design and available QC samples
options.output: Planned QC decisions and a documented analysis table
options.caution: If the study lacks controls, document that limitation. Normalization and exclusion rules need study-specific justification.

stages.title: Molecular annotation
stages.question: Would you like to propose molecular identities?
stages.intro: Candidate formulas, structures and classes are different levels of evidence. The abundance table remains available for later statistics.

options.label: Propose formulas and structure candidates with SIRIUS
options.why: The planned high-resolution precursor-linked spectra can support small-molecule annotation.
options.input: Curated high-accuracy MS/MS export with precursor/adduct information
options.output: Candidate formulas, structures or classes linked back to features
options.caution: Inspect chimeric spectra and export metadata. Web-backed functions require an account/license; candidates are not confirmed identities.

options.label: Leave annotation for later
options.why: You can compare features without claiming their identities.
options.input: Existing planned outputs
options.output: Unannotated features retained

stages.title: Molecular relationships
stages.question: Would a molecular network help your question?
stages.intro: A network groups features with related fragmentation patterns. It complements annotation and does not replace the abundance table.

options.label: Plan feature-based molecular networking
options.why: The paired feature table and representative spectra are the required FBMN inputs.
options.input: Matching quantification table and MGF/MSP spectral summary; optional sample metadata
options.output: Molecular network, spectral-library matches and workflow results
options.caution: Use processor-specific GNPS export conventions. Matching IDs are essential; similarity edges do not confirm structures or biological relationships. A GNPS2 account is needed.

options.label: Continue without networking
options.why: Networking is optional when it does not address the study question.
options.input: Existing planned outputs
options.output: Abundance and annotation outputs retained

stages.title: Statistical analysis
stages.question: How would you like to explore differences between samples?
stages.intro: Return to the QC-reviewed abundance table with sample groups and covariates. Use methods that match replication, pairing and batch structure.

options.label: MetaboAnalyst · browser analysis
options.why: Table-based modules support exploratory and statistical analysis of metabolomics abundances.
options.input: QC-reviewed abundance table formatted for the chosen module, sample labels and covariates
options.output: Statistical results and plots
options.caution: Document missing-value handling, normalization, transformations and multiple testing. Check upload limits and data-sharing rules.

options.label: MetaboAnalystR · scripted analysis
options.why: Use R to record and reproduce table-based statistical choices.
options.input: QC-reviewed abundance matrix and sample metadata in module-specific R structures
options.output: Statistical results, R objects and plots
options.caution: Install the required R dependencies and preserve code, package versions and analysis settings.

options.label: Leave group comparisons out
options.why: Not every dataset has a replicated comparison design.
options.input: Existing planned outputs
options.output: No inferential statistics planned

stages.title: Biological interpretation
stages.question: Plan a careful pathway-mapping review?
stages.intro: Candidate annotation alone does not guarantee usable metabolite identifiers. Check identification confidence, organism, coverage and the measured background first.

options.label: Review identifiers before pathway analysis
options.why: Pathway modules can interpret mapped compounds once identifiers and the study background are suitable.
options.input: Manually reviewed compound IDs, statistical results, organism and measured background
options.output: Conditional pathway-analysis plan and mapping report
options.caution: Stop at identifier review if mapping or evidence is inadequate. Do not substitute feature IDs or predicted classes for identified compounds, and do not equate enrichment with flux.

options.label: Keep interpretation at the feature level
options.why: Avoid pathway claims while identities or database coverage are insufficient.
options.input: Feature-level statistical results
options.output: Prioritized features for follow-up

stages.title: Visualization and reporting
stages.question: Keep the evidence behind the figures.
stages.intro: Use the views and exports from your selected tools. A separated score plot or a convincing network layout is not validation.

options.label: Add an evidence and figure checklist
options.why: Connect figures to feature IDs, processing settings, sample metadata and annotation evidence.
options.input: Selected-tool outputs and the retained feature table
options.output: Planned figures, caption details, uncertainty notes and reproducible settings
options.caution: Record what each figure supports and retain the underlying tables. Avoid interpreting exploratory patterns as established mechanisms.

stages.title: Sharing and reuse
stages.question: How will you preserve the work?
stages.intro: This step plans sharing; nothing is uploaded or made public by Navigator.

options.label: Plan a MassIVE deposition
options.why: A repository can retain MS data, processed outputs and the information needed for reuse.
options.input: Original files where available, processed outputs, sample-to-file mapping and methods
options.output: A planned repository dataset and accession after submission
options.caution: Follow repository submission requirements and confirm permissions before making a dataset public.

options.label: Keep a documented local project for now
options.why: Preserve a reproducible package before deciding on public deposition.
options.input: Available raw data, outputs, metadata, versions and settings
options.output: A documented project archive; no public accession

profiles.name: Cohort study
profiles.summary: Explore associations with participant characteristics or outcomes.
profiles.outline: Sample and participant metadata → processing → QC → association analysis → cautious interpretation
checks: Identify repeated samples from the same participant.
Record relevant covariates, batches and available controls.

guidance.qc: Check sample-to-participant mapping, collection batches and available QC samples.
guidance.statistics: Choose an analysis that accounts for participant independence, covariates and repeated measurements. Group differences alone do not establish causation.

profiles.name: Comparative metabolomics
profiles.outline: Define the comparison → processing → QC → statistical comparison → follow-up
checks: Distinguish independent biological replicates from technical repeats.
Establish whether observations are paired or independent.

guidance.qc: Check replicates, pairing, treatment labels and batch balance before comparing groups.
guidance.statistics: Match the statistical model to pairing, replication and batch structure. With insufficient replication, keep the analysis descriptive.

profiles.name: Natural-product discovery
profiles.summary: Explore molecular families and prioritize compounds for follow-up.
profiles.outline: Processing → QC → annotation → molecular families → candidate prioritization
checks: Record sample provenance and extraction blanks.
Confirm usable MS/MS before planning molecular networking.

guidance.annotation: Prioritize dereplication and annotation evidence. An unmatched spectrum is not proof that a compound is novel.
guidance.network: FBMN can help explore molecular families if matching feature tables and linked MS/MS are available.
guidance.statistics: Group comparisons are optional; only include them if they answer your discovery question.

profiles.name: Bioactivity-guided discovery
profiles.summary: Connect chemical profiles across fractions with assay activity.
profiles.outline: Matched fractions and assays → processing → QC → annotation/networking → activity association
checks: Match chemical profiles and assay measurements to the same fractions.
Check assay controls and plan confirmation of prioritized compounds.

guidance.qc: Preserve fraction IDs shared by chemical data and bioassays; review assay controls alongside chemical QC.
guidance.statistics: This alpha can plan the chemical analysis, but does not yet select a validated activity-correlation implementation. Review that step separately.
guidance.network: Use molecular families as context for activity associations; co-occurrence does not prove that a feature causes activity.

profiles.limitation: The bioactivity-association step requires a separate method review; it is not implemented by this starter.

profiles.name: Explore an existing dataset
profiles.summary: Assess quality and patterns before choosing a specific analysis.
profiles.outline: Identify available files → QC → descriptive exploration → follow-up questions
checks: Identify which processing steps have already been performed.
Check available sample metadata and avoid assuming the table has passed QC.

guidance.start: Choose the files you actually have: original instrument files, mzML or an aligned abundance table.
guidance.statistics: Start with descriptive summaries and quality assessment. Exploratory patterns need follow-up; do not treat them as validated predictions.
